title: Q1 2027 Roadmap & Launch Readiness + Incident Review
topics: Launch readiness checklist for Model Routing + Optimize v2
summary: Internal planning to finalize Q1 priorities, confirm launch readiness for the Model Routing and Redwood Optimize v2 work, and review the recent KV cache/autoscale incident. Agreed on tightened canary, additional load testing, and an action slate for security docs and rollback plan.
action_items: Marcus Chen - Complete canary rollout plan + rollback steps - Due 2027-01-07
Lena Park - Finalize launch checklist and runbooks (inc. who paged) - Due 2026-12-31
Diego Ruiz - Run extended load test with KV caching enabled, capture latency percentiles - Due 2027-01-05
Priya Natarajan - Ship LD (launch doc) and coordinate marketing/CS readiness - Due 2027-01-10
Rowan Ellis - Approve dedicated capacity gating criteria and sign-off for Dedicated customers - Due 2027-01-12
Anya Foster - Provide updated UX notes for the rollout banner and error states - Due 2027-01-04
next_steps: Marcus to share canary playbook and traffic shift schedule in Slack #release-updates
Diego to publish load test results and a follow-up incident mitigation doc
Priya to book cross-functional dry-run on 2027-01-09
Lena to attach final runbooks to the launch checklist in Confluence and link in the LD
competitors_mentioned: internal notes - referenced general cloud AI providers (no specific name)
brief mention of 'other runtimes' by Rowan, no deep competitive analysis
transcript:
[00:00] Priya: alright uh good morning everyone, thanks for joining. the goal today is to close out Q1 planning and make sure we are launch ready for the routing changes and optimize v2. also quick incident postmortem from last week.
[00:18] Marcus: morning, yeah i've got the canary outline, also want to talk about the autoscale thresholds we changed.
[00:32] Lena: quick note, Anya will join for the last ten minutes for the UX banner discussion.
[00:40] Diego: hi all, i pulled the incident logs, i'll walk through the timeline, but TLDR: KV cache eviction pattern + aggressive downscale triggered multi-node cold starts.
[00:55] Rowan: ok let's start with the incident so we don't keep it in our heads while we do roadmap. Diego, timeline?
[01:05] Diego: sure, so on 2026-12-20 around 03:12 UTC we saw a spike in small chat requests that had long context lengths. the cache hit rate dropped from ~89% to ~43% and that caused a bunch of synchronous loads, which together with the recent autoscale config change led to nodes being terminated and then lots of cold starts. the cold starts amplified tail latency.
[01:38] Marcus: right, the recent autoscale tweak was to lower the idle window from 10m to 4m for cost reasons. in hindsight that was too aggressive for that workload variance.
[01:50] Priya: and that was in production for both hosted and dedicated, correct?
[01:55] Diego: yes, hosted and some dedicated pools where we mirrored the policy. some dedicated customers had stricter SLAs and we opened RCAs with them.
[02:05] Lena: transcription note - when Diego said K V cache the transcript had 'kay vee cache' which confused one of the reviewers, heh.
[02:15] Diego: ha, yeah the transcript tends to mangle acronyms. moving on, immediate remediations we applied: increased idle window to 12m, warmed a shadow pool for the worst affected models, and disabled a specific eviction heuristic that was too sensitive.
[02:33] Marcus: the eviction heuristic change reduced memory churn but we need to measure long-term. we should run the extended load tests with a replay of that spike.
[02:44] Priya: agreed. Diego can you run that and capture p50/p95/p99 for token latency?
[02:51] Diego: yes, i'll run it and include KV hit rates and node churn graphs.
[02:58] Rowan: also we need a gating policy for future autoscale changes. we can't just flip on lower idle windows without a canary and SLA check.
[03:10] Marcus: proposed gating: smoke canary at 1% traffic for 2 hours, then ramp to 10% for 24 hours with traffic shadowing and realtime SLO monitors on latency/err rates. if p99 increases by >30% or error rate >0.5% we roll back.
[03:29] Priya: that sounds reasonable. add a rollback play in case model variant fallback is needed.
[03:35] Marcus: yep—include fallback to the previous routing policy and also auto-disable the new heuristic.
[03:41] Lena: switching to roadmap, we have to prioritize between: 1) Model Routing improvements (hot path routing, multi-variant fallback), 2) Redwood Optimize v2 (quantization+batching improvements), and 3) Dedicated autoscale tooling improvements.
[04:00] Priya: my recommendation: push routing improvements and canary playbook to Q1 high priority; Optimize v2 is important but can be staged as beta for select customers; Dedicated autoscale tooling is risk mitigation and should be in parallel but smaller-scope.
[04:19] Marcus: from infra POV routing changes have the highest production blast radius, so we need longer canary and incident runbooks. Optimize v2 changes live more in the runtime pathers (kernel selection), lower blast but more perf testing.
[04:33] Diego: also security gating — KMS changes for key rotation in Optimize v2 path need SOC two sign-off if we touch customer keys.
[04:43] Priya: note, call it 'SOC 2' in docs, the transcript will read 'SOC two' sometimes, which is fine.
[04:52] Rowan: we must be explicit about Dedicated customers: they need an SLA disclosure for potential canary fallout. Marcus, can you define criteria for when a Dedicated customer is allowed into a canary vs excluded?
[05:03] Marcus: yes, propose exclude Dedicated pools with committed throughput >X unless they opt-in and sign a schedule with us; default is opt-out.
[05:12] Priya: let's keep that as a configurable policy in the release checklist.
[05:18] Lena: runbooks — who is owner of the step "who to page if canary fails"? Diego?
[05:23] Diego: i'll own the on-call paging doc and the immediate mitigation steps. Marcus will own rollback.
[05:30] Priya: good. now, launch readiness items: LD (launch doc), runbooks, security checklist (SOC2 + KMS + audit logs), UX messages, customer comms, and load testing.
[05:45] Anya: (joined) hey team, for the UX banner we need copy variants for 'degraded performance' and 'feature rollout' and a small telemetry event for when users see the banner.
[05:56] Priya: great—Anya can you add the telemetry event name to the LD.
[06:01] Anya: yes, i'll add it to the doc.
[06:06] Marcus: load testing scope: full replay of 12/20 spike plus randomized longer context length requests. also validate KV cache warmed state and eviction thresholds. Diego to run, Marcus to review.
[06:18] Diego: noted. i'll set up the replay and a dashboard for quick review.
[06:24] Priya: marketing/CS readiness—i want a one-pager for CS with a FAQ about expected perf changes and a rollback message in case we need to notify customers.
[06:34] Rowan: legal/compliance — any changes that touch customer paddata (PII?) obviously need legal sign-off. are we touching PII?
[06:42] Marcus: no, this work is inference-serving performance. no PII touches. we will still run the security checklist for keys and audit logs.
[06:52] Priya: timeline: we aim to cut the canary on 2027-01-17, dry run on 2027-01-09, and final rollout window 2027-01-24. any objections?
[07:03] Marcus: timeline looks tight but doable if we prioritize the canary playbook and load tests this week.
[07:09] Diego: i can deliver the load test artifacts by 2027-01-05.
[07:13] Lena: i'll finalize the runbooks by 2026-12-31 and link them in the LD.
[07:19] Priya: ok, last bit — incident follow-up items. Diego will publish RCA, include timeline and mitigations. Marcus will stage a config safe-mode that prevents autoscale idle window changes without gating.
[07:32] Marcus: i'll add a feature flag + policy that requires canary approval for idle window changes.
[07:38] Rowan: we should also communicate to the impacted customers next week with the RCA. Priya, can you coordinate with CS?
[07:45] Priya: yes, i'll draft the customer communication and share with legal and CS for review.
[07:51] Anya: one note on UX: we should avoid scary language in banners; prefer "temporary performance adjustments" vs "outage" unless it's an outage.
[07:59] Priya: agreed. any other items?
[08:03] Marcus: just a small ask: can we add a monitoring alert that specifically tracks cache hit-rate by model family? that would have flagged the issue earlier.
[08:12] Diego: i'll add that as an alert and dashboard tile.
[08:16] Rowen: quick spelling, my name is Rowan (small typo in transcript as Rowen earlier).
[08:22] Priya: thanks, ok meeting wrap. recap of owners on action items, post the LD template, and next full dry-run 2027-01-09. thanks everyone.
[08:35] (end)
